subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Cheap Talk and Promises
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Cheap Talk and Promises.

hook.text: Before the game, one player says: I will cooperate. There's no enforcement. Standard theory says ignore it.

buildup.text: Cheap talk is communication that costs nothing and can't be enforced. Theory says it should be ignored since talk.

discovery.text: Experiments show cheap talk works. Pre-play communication increases cooperation substantially, especially face-to-face.

twist.text: Written promises are weaker than spoken ones. Eye contact and vocal tone carry honesty signals that text can't transmit.

climax.text: Humans evolved to detect deception and honor promises. Cheap talk works because breaking a promise has social.

punchline.text: Words are cheap. But breaking them is expensive.

quiz.question: Why does cheap talk increase cooperation despite having no enforcement?
options: People always believe what others say
Breaking a promise has social and psychological costs
The game rules change after communication

details.summary: Cheap talk refers to costless, non-binding communication in strategic settings. Despite having no formal enforcement, cheap talk and promises can influence behavior because people feel social pressure to follow through on stated intentions.
details.whyItMatters: In theory, cheap talk should be ignored since it is costless to lie. In practice, communication dramatically increases cooperation in games like the prisoner's dilemma, revealing that social norms around honesty have real economic value.
takeaways: Cheap talk is communication that is costless and non-binding
Pre-game communication significantly increases cooperation rates
Social norms around promise-keeping give cheap talk real power

faq.question: Why does cheap talk work if lying is costless?
faq.answer: Humans have evolved strong norms around honesty and reciprocity. Breaking a promise creates guilt and reputational damage. Experiments show that even anonymous, one-shot cheap talk increases cooperation because these norms are deeply ingrained.

faq.question: When does cheap talk fail to improve outcomes?
faq.answer: When interests are highly misaligned, when the stakes are very large relative to reputational concerns, or when communication is impersonal. Anonymous online interactions show lower cheap talk effectiveness than face-to-face settings.
